source.title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
source.authors: Xin Chen; Gil Kur; A. Shevchenko; Andreas Krause

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies local-sparsity ideas to instruction-tuned LLMs and reports measurements of sparse SAE representations and local effective dimensions. It does not reproduce the toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and describes superposition as background, but does not measure near-orthogonal directions, feature competition, importance-dependent allocation, or toy-network feature dropping. Its relevant original results measure SAE feature sparsity, local effective dimensions, and overlap of active supports in LLMs. Safety-detector AUROC results are not rows because they measure detector performance rather than the representation claims.
record.test_reason: The paper takes the linear representation hypothesis and superposition as background (cites Elhage et al. 2022). It uses SAEs as a tool for one-class safety detection. Its SAE L0 values are produced by the ReLU plus L1 penalty it imposes, and it reports no reconstruction fidelity. So these values do not show the model contains sparse features an SAE recovers (V4). The d90 and Jaccard measurements concern local sparsity inside an SAE code space it built for detection. That is a different construct from any listed version. The authors state they do not claim SAE features are a good representation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that local sparsity (shared active SAE supports within neighbourhoods, low local effective dimension) makes unsupervised one-class LLM safety detection feasible. Their detectors are competitive with one-class baselines, at a 0.04–0.08 AUROC gap to a supervised probe. With 1% labeled calibration, AUROC reaches about 0.96–0.99. They give a sample-complexity bound that is logarithmic in SAE width, do not claim robustness to adaptive attacks, and explicitly do not claim SAE features are a good representation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on LLM residual-stream activations and measures local active supports and PCA effective dimensions; it does not use the toy-model intervention or geometric measurements of the original superposition study.
record.method_sensitivity: Local effective dimension and detection behavior vary by model and mask construction. SAE sparsity depends on training penalty and training length. The paper reports model-dependent mask sizes and extraction-layer effects; the layer used in the main analysis is not the best on Gemma-4-26B among the tested layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Within K-means clusters of SAE codes, the per-cluster top-k masked subspace has low PCA d90 (median 17.5–40.5 across five models, vs raw SAE 43–126). Safe and unsafe inputs share near-identical majority-active supports (Jaccard median ≥0.94).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local sparsity: SAE codes of nearby LLM inputs share a small common active support, with low local effective dimension.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The evidence is limited to six instruction-tuned model families and selected layers and SAEs. Per-cluster d90 results are reported for five families; Gemma-4-26B is omitted because its selected mask has k = 25. The paper cautions that empirical d90 is not a population concentration bound and its theory treats the SAE as given rather than analyzing SAE training. The measurements do not establish SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result rows left out.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition measured.
Whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs faithfully recover model features. No reconstruction or fidelity results are reported; SAE sparsity is imposed by the L1 penalty.
All: completeness, stability and canonicality are not evaluated. The authors disclaim that SAE features are a good representation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. L0 sparsity is enforced by the L1 objective and varies with λ and epochs. The d90 and Jaccard results concern the detector's own local subspaces. The statement that 'larger models pack more concepts' is an untested interpretation of mask gains on GPT-oss and Gemma. Paper is code-released and NeurIPS 2026.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity and competition for capacity between features of different importance.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.

The study measures SAE sparsity and local support structure, but does not establish that SAE features are a complete account of model representations or quantify how features are distributed across individual neurons.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features are not evaluated.
The dimensionality of individual represented features is not tested.

rows.note: The paper says this is the encoder used for the main results.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Measured SAE representations and local masks in the reported instruction-tuned LLM settings
reader_labels.reason: The reported SAE densities are sparse, local d90 is low relative to the 16384-dimensional SAE space in five families, and safe/unsafe active supports have high within-cluster overlap (r1-r9, r20-r25).
